applicableAreas: demolition operations near transmission facilities
findings.comment: Demolition plan notes do not address required safety clearances from transmission lines: pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy 48 hours before work commencement, barricades erected 10 feet from transmission structures, warning signs under overhead facilities, and prohibition on materials or spoils storage within transmission easement. Sheet 3 (General Notes) specifies transmission facility requirements but Sheet 8 demolition notes (Block 9, 10 items) do not reference or incorporate these safety requirements.

applicableAreas: demolition work areas near at-grade utility appurtenances
findings.comment: Demolition plan general notes (Sheet 8, Block 9) do not include a note requiring contractor to exercise extreme caution when working near at-grade utility appurtenances (meter boxes, cleanouts, valve boxes, pump stations, service pedestals, etc.). This standard precaution is required on all demolition plans with proposed utility infrastructure.

applicableAreas: biofiltration/detention pond maintenance access drive
findings.comment: SCM maintenance access drive vertical clearance is not documented at minimum 14 feet from existing and proposed vegetation and all other objects. Sheet 16 maintenance and construction requirements (Block 8) address tree preservation in the access drive design but do not specify the 14-foot minimum vertical clearance requirement from vegetation at maturity and all other overhead obstructions.

applicableAreas: utility plan sheets, site plan sheets, electrical design plan
findings.comment: Overhead electrical clearance zones are not graphically delineated on plans. Distribution clearance envelope boundaries (7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial zone from outside conductor) are not shown on site plan or utility plan sheets. No transmission clearance envelope (which requires AE-provided site-specific analysis) is shown despite Sheet 3 referencing transmission facilities.

applicableAreas: utility plan sheets, site plan, grading plan
findings.comment: Horizontal dashed height limit lines are not shown on plans to delineate AE overhead conductor clearance envelope boundaries. Site plan, grading plan, and utility plan sheets lack the required height limit line annotations that establish the vertical boundary of the overhead utility clearance zones.

applicableAreas: utility plan sheets, grading plan profiles
findings.comment: Sloped or stepped dashed height limit lines are not shown on plans where overhead utilities are present on sites with non-uniform grade conditions. The site has sloped terrain (elevations ranging from ~678.5' to ~681' per benchmarks), but no profile-view height limit lines reflecting grade changes beneath overhead conductor spans are depicted on grading plan or utility profile sheets.

applicableAreas: overhead electric lines along western and southern site boundaries
findings.comment: Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from AE overhead primary, neutral, or secondary conductors cannot be verified. Overhead electric lines (OHE) are shown on the electrical plan and site plan along Valley View Road boundary, but no clearance dimension lines or measurements are provided from the outermost conductor to any customer facility edge, building, transformer pad, or other structure.

applicableAreas: overhead electric lines along western and southern site boundaries
findings.comment: Minimum 15-foot radial clearance from AE overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors cannot be verified. No radial clearance envelopes, dimension arcs, or measurements are shown on utility plan or site plan sheets from the outside conductor to any proposed customer facility.

applicableAreas: utility tap vault (if proximate to overhead utilities)
findings.comment: Vault vertical clearance from top of proposed structure to sag of lowest overhead power line is not labeled on plans. Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 20) indicates a fire demand meter vault connection but does not show or dimension its vertical proximity to the overhead electric line shown along Valley View Road. No Austin Energy written clearance approval letter is evident in the project file documentation reviewed.

applicableAreas: all areas where clearance measurements are shown
findings.comment: Clearance dimension lines cannot be verified as anchored to outermost conductor rather than utility pole centerline. No clearance dimensions are shown on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) or site plan (Sheet 9) to verify proper measurement reference points.

applicableAreas: electrical transformer pads and electrical meters
findings.comment: Customer service entrance facilities and electrical appurtenances are not documented with minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from AE poles and overhead lines other than service drop. Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations and electrical meter locations but provides no horizontal clearance dimension lines from these facilities to the OHE line or power poles shown along the property boundary.

applicableAreas: utility crossings between water/wastewater and electrical infrastructure
findings.comment: AE underground facility clearance from other utilities at perpendicular crossings cannot be verified with the required 12-inch minimum. Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile (Sheet 20) shows the proposed water line tap connection but does not label horizontal or vertical clearance dimensions between the water line and any AE underground electrical conduit at crossing points.

applicableAreas: utility tap connection location in Valley View Road right-of-way
findings.comment: Proposed utility located within 24 inches of existing ROW facility cannot be verified with AULCC ROW assignment change approval documentation. Sheet 20 shows utility tap proximity to existing water main but does not reference AULCC Completeness Letter (ROW assignment change approval) or other formal AULCC authorization in the plan notes or project documentation reviewed.

applicableAreas: water/wastewater utility crossings
findings.comment: Utility crossing method (trenchless vs. open-cut) cannot be clearly identified on plans, preventing verification of applicable separation standard. Sheet 20 utility tap profile does not explicitly state whether the proposed water line tap crossing under Valley View Road or existing water main is trenchless or open-cut, which determines whether UCM 2.9.2.B.17 (trenchless: 36 in or 2× diameter) or UCM 2.9.1.B.3 (open-cut: 12-18 in) applies.

applicableAreas: utilities crossing under Valley View Road
findings.comment: Encasement specifications are not provided for utilities crossing under roadways or structures. Utility Tap Plan & Profile (Sheet 20) does not reference or detail encasement material type, dimensions, or longitudinal extent specifications for the proposed utility tap crossing under Valley View Road.

applicableAreas: wastewater cleanout locations
findings.comment: Large-diameter cleanout horizontal clearance from utility poles and guy wires cannot be verified. Construction Details Sheet 26 shows wastewater cleanout specifications but does not provide horizontal clearance dimensions from proposed cleanout locations to existing AE utility poles or guy wires on the site.

applicableAreas: storm drain manhole locations
findings.comment: Storm drain manhole horizontal clearance from Austin Energy overhead electric poles cannot be verified with the required 5-foot minimum. Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12) depicts multiple storm drain manholes across the site but does not provide horizontal clearance dimension lines from manhole locations to the AE power poles shown along the western and southern property boundaries.

applicableAreas: transmission structures and water easements (if present and identifiable)
findings.comment: Electric utility poles proposed within water easements or within 10 feet of large electric transmission structures cannot be verified because transmission structures are not depicted on any site plan sheet or plat, despite Sheet 3 containing 16 detailed Electric Transmission Notes referencing transmission easements and structures. Applicability and compliance cannot be determined without clear identification of transmission facility location.

applicableAreas: transmission ROW access corridor (if transmission facilities exist)
findings.comment: Maintenance of 25-foot-wide transmission ROW access corridor with 16-foot minimum vertical clearance cannot be verified. Although Sheet 3 contains detailed transmission facility requirements, no transmission ROW or access corridor is graphically depicted or dimensioned on site plan (Sheet 9) or construction/staging plans to demonstrate the required 25-foot width and 16-foot vertical clearance for its full length.

applicableAreas: biofiltration/detention pond staging area
findings.comment: SCM staging area vertical clearance minimum 14 feet from existing and proposed vegetation and all other objects cannot be verified. Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan (Sheet 15) addresses pond design and storage volumes but does not specify a designated staging area with labeled 14-foot vertical clearance dimensions from overhead vegetation and other objects.

applicableAreas: work zone and construction access driveway below overhead electric lines
findings.comment: Work zone or construction access driveway vertical clearance below overhead utilities cannot be verified. Overhead electric line (OHE) is shown along the western and southern site boundaries on the site plan, but no vertical clearance dimensions are documented at internal driveway access points or work zones that may pass beneath overhead conductor spans.

applicableAreas: staging and temporary spoils areas
findings.comment: Staging or temporary spoils areas overlapping utility line alignments or transmission easement cannot be verified. Although Sheet 3 specifies transmission easement restrictions (no spoils within 25 feet of transmission structures), a detailed staging/construction plan layout is not available in the reviewed sheets to confirm that staging areas avoid utility alignments and transmission easement encroachment.
